model_interpretation.claim: Using a zero-based x index from line pointers already positioned at x0 avoids applying the interior offset twice and presents a contiguous loop to the compiler. Prior valid OpenMP SIMD candidates show this directive is supported in the measured build; checking the actual input, velocity, and output line starts enables an aligned SIMD path only when all three satisfy the 16-byte condition, with an unaligned SIMD fallback. The guarded, unpeeled formulation is distinct from prior scalar peeling variants, and its performance remains to be measured.

items.subject: Single-sweep x-line kernel vectorization
items.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, isolate the unfused single-timestep kernel and contiguous-x line traversal. Compare the existing scalar formulation with compiler-vectorizable and, only if supported by the frozen build, explicit SIMD formulations; do not change compiler flags or assume an ISA extension. Account for the interior start offset despite aligned inputs. Keep threading and spatial/temporal blocking out of scope. Preserve numerical tolerance and boundaries; validate and measure the kernel under the official settings.
